findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed food items such as but not limited to lettuce heads and other vegetables stored on the floor of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC and vegetables were placed on shelves. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches from the floor or in a manner that protects against contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: During the inspection, an employee was observed to wash their hands and shut off the faucet without using a barrier. This heavier was corrected on site and the employee rewashed their hands with correct procedure. PIC will retrain staff on hand washing. Ensure staff wash their hands following correct hand washing procedures. 
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: 
-The gaskets of the refrigerators and freezers in the kitchen are observed to have an accumulation of dust/food debris. Ensure the current accumulation of dust/food debris is cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
-The white shelving above the triple sink is observed to have an accumulation of dust and is in need of being cleaned. Ensure that the shelving is cleaned of the current accumulation and then is cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The wall panel directly above the triple sink is observed to have an apparent gap present where the panel has lifted away from the wall. Ensure this panel is repaired or replaced to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface. 
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: The mop is observed to be stored with the mop head directly on the floor and unable to air dry. This mop was inverted and placed in a position able to air dry during the inspection. Ensure the mop is stored in a manner that allows it to air dry between uses.
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:

Ensure these surfaces are cleaned to remove the current buildup of accumulation and then ensure these surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: The top of the white freezer next to the microwave is observed to have an excessive accumulation of dust/soil debris. On this surface is stored single service to-go containers. The bottom container is being discarded during today’s inspection and the sing service items are being moved from this location and will not be stored on this surface until it is cleaned and sanitized. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: The shelf in the back corner of the kitchen that holds the bowls is currently covered with contact paper that is heavily damaged and soiled. The bowls are not in contact with the paper on the food contact surface and so the facility has been advised to remove the contact paper and either change it out with new paper that is changed at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean or to remove the contact paper and replace it with a plastic or metal sheeting that is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was tested at 0ppm chlorine at the waiting area. Bleach was added to the sanitizer solution which brought the concentration up to 100ppm chlorine. Ensure test strips are used to test and verify that the sanitizer solution meets requirements.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The walk-in cooler was recorded at 58 degrees F at the start of the inspection. The cooler was observed in operating order during the hours of prep before the facility opened today which was less than 4 hours ago. The food items requiring cold holding below 41 degrees F and the eggs which require under 45 degrees F were moved into the white fridge along the cook line that was holding temperature. No food items remain in the cooler that are potentially hazardous at this time. Observation of the cooler will be made towards the end of the inspection to observe the temperature again. If records show the cooler above 41 degrees F, main entrance is required on the cooler. Facility has stated they will monitor the temperature again in the morning and call for service at that time if necessary.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.
